title: The blocked Copacabana contract in Rio and the band's decline
summary: The band had a one-year Rio de Janeiro contract just as the war began but were not allowed to leave the country, which started the band's downgrade as members were lost.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: This was immediately when the war broke out.

And if you remember, Nelson Rockefeller was in charge of Latin affairs at that time, and so we went around and we all did this together, Kirby and everybody, and we pulled all sorts of strings to get out of the country, down on this job. Because we had it all figured out. We could go down there, and I think it was a year, like we'd all go down there and continue exactly what we were doing and come back rich. Not rich, but well on our way, because you know, we were young at that time and you know, most of the fellows in the band weren't even 30 years old yet. You must remember that too. I think Buster was the oldest. I think he was 32 or 3, something like that. So you see we had it all in front of us. But we weren't allowed to leave the country.

But I don't know whether they thought that we just wanted to leave the country because of the war, on account of the war, you know. But the more we pursued, you know, what we wanted to do, it seemed the deeper the hole we were digging. Then the word got around to all the draft boards and everybody, about who's this bunch of people who want to -- you know, collectively. So it never came off. And that was the first inkling or the first happening that started the band on a downgrade, because Billy left, and the war and whatever, and seriously though, I don't think that Kirby -- when all this happened, I don't think Kirby could cope with the situation. You know, the wartime, because he could have done -- he tried it, like every other bandleader did -- if one of the members of band had to join the armed forces, he just got somebody else to replace him. But it wasn't so easy in the John Kirby Band, see, because the band was so tight and so well-organized and -- that it wasn't easy to. Because even -- now, somebody put out a John Kirby thing, an album or something, and it's full of all these before and after stuff, and when I say John Kirby's band, I mean just that group that formed the band and made it.
